status: No default-search integration or manuscript numerical update
execution: Four runs executed sequentially; no concurrent experiment launched by this study. Other desktop workloads remained active.
order: Alternating full/local and local/full, balanced across repetitions
aggregation: Take each query's median repeated wall time for each path, then summarize paired ratios across queries. Setup is a separate single measurement of region construction plus support remapping. Memory uses each query's maximum incremental allocation over repetitions, then the median across queries.
interpretation: Local evaluation reduces transient tensor allocation substantially, but median timing including setup is slower in every run for this three-support batch. Excluding setup, observed paired median ratios range from about 1.00 to 1.65. These results do not establish faster explanation search.
limitations: Shared-device and host scheduling effects are not controlled; absolute times differ substantially across runs. Do not pool them into an end-to-end speed claim.
Timing covers retain/delete forwards for three already-selected supports, not gradient proposals, acceptance checks, spectral preprocessing or the full search workload.
Incremental allocated-memory peaks exclude persistent model, original graph and preconstructed local graph storage. They are not total GPU peak memory or reserved-memory measurements.
Repeated timings and query budgets are not independent experimental runs.
Amortization of setup across search steps and adaptive-trajectory changes remain unmeasured.
decision: Keep compaction opt-in. Its current supported benefit is transient-memory reduction. Before integration, measure complete search including construction and full-graph acceptance checks; do not substitute node-count ratios for measured speedups.
